---
title: "Documentation and sharing"
subtitle: "Cheat sheet for lessons 11 and 12"
---

## Seven questions a README answers

1. What is this project about?
2. Is there a publication related to it?
3. What is in this repository?
4. What hardware does it need?
5. How do I reproduce the analyses? (one command: `pixi run reproduce`)
6. What outputs should I expect?
7. How can I contact the authors or discuss the project?

See [lesson 11, section 1](../pages/11-documentation.qmd#what-a-reader-needs-to-know).

## Files a reader looks for

| File | What it says |
|------------|------------------------|
| `README.md` | the seven answers |
| `LICENSE` | what others may do with your work |
| `CITATION.cff` | how to cite it (GitHub shows a *Cite this repository* button) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` | how to take part |
| `docs/software-versions.txt` | the exact software, from the lock file |

## Licenses

| Material | Common choice |
|------------|------------------------|
| Code | MIT, BSD-3-Clause or Apache-2.0 (permissive); GPL-3.0 (copyleft) |
| Text, figures, slides | CC BY 4.0 |
| Data | CC0 or CC BY 4.0 |
| Avoid for open research | Creative Commons "NC" and "ND" licenses |

You can only license what you own. See [section 4](../pages/11-documentation.qmd#licenses-what-others-may-do).

## Commands

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| How much disk space the project needs | `du -sh .pixi/envs/* data/raw results` |
| Check `CITATION.cff` | `pixi exec cffconvert --validate -i CITATION.cff` |
| The citation as APA or BibTeX | `pixi exec cffconvert -i CITATION.cff -f apalike` (or `-f bibtex`) |
| Software versions for the README | `pixi list -e pipeline --explicit > docs/software-versions.txt` |
| A picture of the workflow | `pixi run -e pipeline snakemake --rulegraph > docs/rulegraph.dot`, then `pixi run -e pipeline dot -Tsvg docs/rulegraph.dot -o docs/rulegraph.svg` |
| Test it like a stranger would | `git clone git@github.com:USER/REPO.git FOLDER`, then in it `pixi install --locked` and `pixi run reproduce` |
| Tag the version you release | `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "MESSAGE"`, then `git push origin v1.0.0` |

## A minimal `CITATION.cff`

```{.yaml}
cff-version: 1.2.0
message: "If you use this work, please cite it as below."
title: "LTEE variant calling"
type: software
authors:
  - given-names: "Ada"
    family-names: "Lovelace"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097"
repository-code: "https://github.com/ada-lovelace/ltee-project"
license: MIT
version: 1.0.0
date-released: "2026-12-01"
```

An ORCID iD must be the full URL. See [section 5](../pages/11-documentation.qmd#a-citation-file).

## A release with a DOI (Zenodo)

1. Log in to Zenodo with GitHub (practise on <https://sandbox.zenodo.org/> first).
2. In Zenodo's *GitHub* page, press *Sync* and switch on your repository.
3. Check that `CITATION.cff` is valid: Zenodo takes the title, authors and license from it.
4. Tag and push the version, then on GitHub: *Releases → Draft a new release*, pick the tag, *Publish release*.
5. Copy the DOI and its badge from Zenodo into the README and `CITATION.cff`.

See [lesson 12, section 3](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd#release-and-archive-on-zenodo), and the
[checklist for your next project](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd#a-checklist-for-your-next-project).

## Official cheat sheets and references

There is no official cheat sheet for documenting and releasing research
code. The official references for each part:

- Citation File Format, *Guide to the schema* (every `CITATION.cff` key): <https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/blob/main/schema-guide.md>
- GitHub Docs, *Referencing and citing content* (Zenodo and GitHub releases): <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/archiving-a-github-repository/referencing-and-citing-content>
- Zenodo, *GitHub integration*: <https://help.zenodo.org/docs/github/>
- choosealicense.com, software licenses in plain language (from GitHub): <https://choosealicense.com/>
- cffconvert, the validator used above: <https://github.com/citation-file-format/cffconvert>
